podcast.body: Released in 1979, this song was conceived after Gary Numan, originally a guitar enthusiast, discovered a Mini-Moog in a studio and decided to write punk songs using electronic instrumentation. The lyrics are based on his vision of a future where machines called "friends" provide services, with the friend in the song specifically depicted as a prostitute. It became a massive hit, selling over a million copies in the UK. "He called these machines friends, and the friend in this song is supposed to be a prostitute."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in June 1979, this track hit number one on the British charts and became a significant hit in North America, effectively initiating the Technopop era. "That's Gary Newman with our friends, electric, from June of 1979. ... That was the track that really kicked off the Technopop era when it hit number one on the British charts that also became a sizeable hit in North America."

podcast.body: This is a cover version of Gary Numan's original song, featured as the B-side on a 7-inch record with the catalog number TMR001. The record was purchased from Third Man Records. "It's a cover of Gary Newman's Our Friends Electric."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is one of Gary Numan's new wave technopop hits that emerged after he decided to abandon guitars, influenced by the unique capabilities of the Mini-Moog. It exemplifies the electronic sound he pioneered. "A Mini-Mog left unattended in a studio, inspired Gary Newman to give up on guitars completely, resulting in new wave technopop hits like Cars and our friends electric."
